races.name: Ocean Scotland Outdoor Advertising Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bea Kindly
runners_data.note: Tracy Waggott's filly has returned form figures of 9-6-9 and her historical runs show no win or place; 66 days off the track is a concern for a two-year-old, and while she is a natural hold-up type her tendency to fade in the finish makes this compact 5f trip on a fast surface an unkind ask.

runners_data.name: Claret And Blues
runners_data.note: Fahey yard have had four winners from 44 runners in the past 14 days suggesting current form, and this filly has a 3/5f placing on standard going; she runs hold-up by nature but her most recent 5f run produced a third, hinting she can quicken when the race unfolds cleanly.

runners_data.name: Enemy Action
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears saddles this hold-up runner whose best effort — a third over 5f on good ground — is the most encouraging piece of recent form in the hold-up group; Harry Russell's booking is noted, and 17 days between runs is a standard turnaround, leaving him likely to be the most competitive off-pace threat here.

runners_data.name: Lairy Mary
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's filly is the only confirmed front-runner in the field and her one win came over 5f on good ground, directly mirroring today's conditions; racing in her natural position with zero pace pressure is the key angle, though she carries 134lbs and her form string shows inconsistency when not able to dictate.

runners_data.name: Mr Darling
runners_data.note: Bryan Smart's colt has finished sixth or worse in all four career starts, including three consecutive last-placed efforts over 5f on good ground; the lowest OR in the field at 46 reflects his consistent struggles, and the style-fit discount applies as a hold-up runner who will need traffic to clear — which may not materialise.

runners_data.name: Stripes Of Glory
runners_data.note: David Allan takes the ride for the Easterby yard and this colt is 66 days fresh, having finished no better than sixth in three starts; a natural hold-up type whose form at Musselburgh distances mirrors today's trip, though his style-fit discount and lack of any win or place means he is relying on others to underperform.

races.paceDynamic: Lairy Mary is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 5f nursery handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should settle comfortably on the front end and control the tempo from the off on good-to-firm ground at Musselburgh. Behind her, Claret And Blues, Enemy Action, Bea Kindly, Mr Darling, and Stripes Of Glory are all hold-up types by inclination, meaning the race is structured around one pace-setter and a clutch of closers — a dynamic that gives Lairy Mary a significant tactical advantage. The uncontested lead on a flat, tight 5f track in good-to-firm conditions creates an ideal platform for a front-runner to dictate, compress the pace into manageable fractions, and force those chasing to produce sustained, attritional finishing efforts rather than a single late burst. This race shape overwhelmingly favours the hold-your-position, front-running profile, with Lairy Mary uniquely positioned to exploit it. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically find a clean run from the rear simultaneously; of the redistributed group, Enemy Action and Claret And Blues — who have shown some positional flexibility in their histories — are most likely to push forward and secure a prominent tracking position behind the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lairy Mary Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lairy Mary hacks to the front uncontested and sets a controlled, confidence-boosting gallop.
scenarios.body: Lairy Mary dictates every yard on the good-to-firm surface, never burning herself out early, and the hold-up horses behind are forced to pick their way through without a true searching test of the pace ahead; on a flat 5f track she simply does not give them enough time or ground to reel her in. The front-running profile is uniquely suited here, and Lairy Mary's one career win came over 5f on good ground, validating the match between horse and conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Lairy Mary's controlled pace still sets up a sprint finish that a well-placed hold-up runner exploits from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Musselburgh's flat straight gives closers a chance if the winner times a run to perfection, and a horse like Enemy Action — who has placed over 5f on good ground — could latch onto the leader's quarters turning for home and just outlast her. The gap in class and OR between front and back of the field is narrow enough that the right trajectory from a mid-position runner could find the wire first.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Lairy Mary over-extends herself fractionally and the gap narrows sharply in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Good-to-firm conditions can occasionally catch a free-going front-runner if she has misjudged her own fractions, and with five horses all capable of finishing into a tired leader the closing stages could compress dramatically. The true hold-up types — Bea Kindly and Stripes Of Glory — benefit most from this scenario, though both carry the caveat that their form strings show consistent late fading and low-ranked finishes.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Traffic Issues
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses bunch in a narrow group, creating interference that scrambles the natural running order entirely.
scenarios.body: With five closers all seeking room simultaneously on a 5f straight, traffic problems and checking movements are plausible, potentially gifting a clear-passage runner an advantage they would not otherwise hold. Mr Darling, though consistently outclassed, could benefit from an entirely clean passage if the field bunches and creates clear daylight on one rail.

watchPoints.text: Watch Lairy Mary's early behaviour — if she is allowed to bowl along uncontested inside the first furlong, she controls the shape of the entire race and the probability of SCENARIO_A rises sharply.

Monitor where Enemy Action and Claret And Blues pitch up in the early stages — if either pushes forward to track Lairy Mary, the pace context shifts and the closing group loses its most likely finisher.

Bea Kindly's 66-day absence combined with her pattern of fading late means she is a horse to watch for signs of rustiness in the first two furlongs; a flat early effort would confirm she is not a factor today.

With five hold-up types competing for the same ground on a flat 5f straight, watch the draw and rail positions at the start — a horse drawn widest with a clean passage could outperform its OR rating simply by avoiding the likely cluster in midfield.

Track the going underfoot through the afternoon card; multiple reports list conditions as good-to-firm, which strongly favours the front-runner's stamina and makes it harder for hold-up horses to produce a decisive late surge.

races.name: Mr & Mrs McKinlay Wedding Anniversary Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Arrange
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer for Martin Todhunter and David Nolan, 29 days off but solid similar-going form (10/15 runners placed), needs the pace to be honest enough over 2m to launch a late run — the controlled fractions Lagoon Nebula is likely to set may blunt that chance.

runners_data.name: Cascade Hall
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's seven-year-old returns quickly (8 days) in fine form (three runs: 3rd, 4th, 3rd) with strong 2W/5P placed record on similar going, and as a true hold-up type has the class profile to finish well if the pace builds sufficiently in the straight.

runners_data.name: Lagoon Nebula
runners_data.note: Andrew Kinirons' five-year-old is the sole confirmed front-runner here and will enjoy a clear lead, but the STYLE_FIT flag notes they are racing somewhat out of their most comfortable role; their chance depends on whether that controlled lead is sustainable over the full 2m on quick ground.

runners_data.name: Max Of Stars
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears' six-year-old has the best similar-going record in the field (12/15, 3W/7P) and claims a five-pound allowance via Tom Kiely-Marshall; a natural prominent racer who has won and placed over 2m on similar going repeatedly, this race shape suits them well.

runners_data.name: Mr Withington
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans' five-year-old has a modest 0W/0P record on similar going and has finished no higher than sixth in his last five; in truth a hold-up horse whose real position will be further back than the map reflects, making him heavily dependent on a pace scenario that is unlikely to materialise here.

runners_data.name: Newport
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's six-year-old has a win and two places from ten similar-going starts and was placed twice over 2m on Good ground in recent form; a prominent racer with the tactical speed to track Lagoon Nebula and the stamina to sustain it, this flat-track setup is a good match.

runners_data.name: Speechman
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's six-year-old carries the lowest OR in the field and is tagged as a fader in the finish; genuinely a hold-up type placed further forward on the map only by distribution pressure, and with 0W/2P on similar going and a trend of regressing late in races, this shape is unflattering.

races.paceDynamic: Lagoon Nebula is the lone confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 2m handicap on Good to Firm ground at Musselburgh, and with no genuine rival to press them early, they are set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. Newport and Max Of Stars are the natural prominent racers likely to track Lagoon Nebula through the early and middle stages, giving the pace some shape without generating a true test of stamina. Cascade Hall and Arrange sit at the back of the field as genuine hold-up types, needing the pace to be sufficient over two miles to allow them to deliver a late run — on a flat track with a single unhurried front-runner, that delivery is not guaranteed. Mr Withington and Speechman are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because this field carries more off-the-pace types than can all slot naturally at the rear; in reality they are unlikely to be closer to the pace than their natural style suggests, and their chance depends on a scenario that is harder to construct here. The race shape strongly favours a horse sitting prominently or just off the pace in second or third, able to press Lagoon Nebula turning for home and sustain their effort to the line — prominent racers with proven form at the trip on similar going are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls All
scenarios.trigger: If Lagoon Nebula dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the field never applies meaningful pressure before the home straight.
scenarios.body: Lagoon Nebula sets fractions that suit a prominent racer tracking in second or third, and whichever of Newport or Max Of Stars travels smoothly in their slipstream is best positioned to challenge and sustain a run to the line on this flat circuit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Poacher Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Newport or Max Of Stars moves to challenge Lagoon Nebula before the home turn, lifting the tempo and turning it into a genuine stamina test from three furlongs out.
scenarios.body: The increased pace suits horses who have shown they can travel prominently and grind, and the extended run-in at Musselburgh rewards those hitting the front early with sustained momentum.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If Lagoon Nebula's uncontested lead paradoxically results in a fast finishing burst in the straight that rewards those held up for one strong run.
scenarios.body: Cascade Hall and Arrange, genuine hold-up types with solid form on similar going, would be the primary beneficiaries if the pace quickens sharply and the front-runners are caught out late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the Good to Firm ground rides quicker than expected, the pace collapses or one of the prominent horses surges wide, fragmenting the field and creating an unsettled shape.
scenarios.body: In this muddled scenario lower-weighted, fresh horses with recent course experience or resilient form strings could profit from rivals tiring at unexpected moments.

watchPoints.text: Newport and Max Of Stars — watch which of these prominent types gets closest to Lagoon Nebula's early position, as the one that tracks the leader most smoothly through the first mile is best placed to strike turning for home.

Lagoon Nebula — if they are allowed to stride into an uncontested lead of more than three lengths by halfway, the absence of any genuine pressing challenger means the race could be over well before the straight, compressing the chance of all hold-up horses.

Cascade Hall — returns on just 8 days' rest and is a true closer; monitor in-running positioning closely, as if they are further back than usual in a slowly-run race their strong recent form may count for little.

Mr Withington and Speechman — both are genuine hold-up horses effectively buried in the pack; if either appears to be tracking more prominently than expected in the early stages it would represent a meaningful change of tactics worth noting for future reference.

Going — officially Good to Firm for this race per the going report; any drying that makes it ride faster than expected could sharpen the pace and bring the closers back into play, particularly benefiting Cascade Hall and Arrange.

races.name: Celebrating The Musselburgh Festival 2026 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Black Storm
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Katie Scott trained well at this track, finishing 2nd over 7f on Good 12 days ago — consistent in similar conditions with four placings from 15 similar-ground runs, but needs a proper pace injection to deliver her challenge.|

runners_data.name: Carolus Magnus
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this well-seasoned 8-year-old for Easterby, who carries excellent course-and-distance form including a recent 7f Good win; prominent style suits this race shape neatly and he is a live contender.|

runners_data.name: Keep Me Stable
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's 6-year-old is a genuine front-runner by nature — three wins from 15 similar-ground starts — but with Lady Gormire dominating the lead and multiple prominent types ahead, he is likely to settle into a midfield berth that is not his preferred operating zone, tempering his chance.|

runners_data.name: Supreme Clarets
runners_data.note: Fahey's 3-year-old has placed twice on Good ground over 7f but has yet to win — hold-up profile means he requires the pace to set things up for him, and a controlled Lady Gormire gallop may not provide the gaps he needs.|

runners_data.name: The Gay Blade
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 7-year-old arrives in excellent heart with three wins in his last five including two at 7f on Good, and a prominent style that is perfectly suited to travelling close to Lady Gormire's measured pace throughout.|

runners_data.name: We've Got This
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's 4-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by inclination, but with other closers also filling the rear positions, Tom Eaves may find him racing marginally closer than ideal — the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 reflects a real positional compromise here.|

runners_data.name: Yaaser
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 8-year-old is winless in his last 15 similar-ground starts and Paul Mulrennan will likely tuck him in somewhere in the pack; his true back-of-field role is squeezed by the cluster of hold-up types, meaning he may not get the rail-creeping position he favours.|

runners_data.name: Lady Gormire
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's 3-year-old holds all four strongest cards in this race shape — she sets the pace, controls the fractions, has consecutive placings on Good ground including a recent 2nd over 7f, and faces no challenger for the front.|

runners_data.name: Masaban
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's 3-year-old has a win on Good ground over a mile and consecutive placings at 7f on Good, and his prominent style places him directly in the prime tracking position — the yard is in decent form at 7/32 over 14 days.|

runners_data.name: Napolian
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 3-year-old drops back to 7f after a disappointing 0 last time, but his earlier form at 6f-8f on Good includes a win and multiple placings; a prominent runner who could benefit from a compressed, steady early gallop.|

runners_data.name: No Return
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's 4-year-old has a strong record on similar ground with two wins and four placings but all his best form has come at 6f — stretching to 7f here is a genuine query, and his hold-up style makes him reliant on a strong pace he may not get today.|

races.paceDynamic: Lady Gormire is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 7f handicap and, with no genuine rival to push her for the lead, she should be able to control a comfortable, sustainable gallop from the front on Good to Firm ground. Carolus Magnus, The Gay Blade, Masaban, and Napolian will all push to hold prominent positions just behind her, creating a compact but organised early order rather than a chaotic battle for the front. The field contains more prominent-profile horses than the map can accommodate cleanly — Keep Me Stable is a genuine front-runner by nature who will likely be forced to settle closer to midfield than he would prefer, while We've Got This and Yaaser are true hold-up horses who may find themselves unable to drop as far back as ideally suited. With Lady Gormire dictating an uncontested, measured pace on fast ground over 7f, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel close to the action and pounce in the straight without needing a strong injection of pace to bring them into it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gormire Dictates, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Gormire leads at a controlled pace and the race is decided by horses close to her from the outset.
scenarios.body: Lady Gormire sets a steady, uncontested tempo and the race becomes a test of quality for those racing just behind her in the first three to four, with the straight at Musselburgh providing the decisive stretch for those who have saved energy through a measured early gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Front Runner Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Gormire is pressured early or deliberately ups the tempo, turning this into a true test of stamina and front-running resolution.
scenarios.body: A stronger early pace suits a front-runner with the fitness and class to sustain it, and Lady Gormire's recent consistent placing record suggests she may have enough to hold on if the gallop is honest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final 2f after an honest gallop and genuine late runners find clear daylight on the wide Musselburgh straight.
scenarios.body: A true late-running profile would benefit from this shape, but several of the hold-up types in this field have been displaced from their natural position and may not deliver the expected sustained finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Pace, Midfield Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively slow throughout and horses tracking in mid-division between the leaders and the closers steal the advantage.
scenarios.body: A slow-run 7f on quick ground can compress the field and reward horses sitting third or fourth who nick a gap in the straight before the true hold-up horses can wind up.

watchPoints.text: Lady Gormire's ability to control the fractions unchallenged is the single biggest factor shaping this race — watch whether any of the prominent runners, particularly The Gay Blade or Napolian, push up aggressively in the opening furlong and force a faster early pace than she wants.

Keep Me Stable's jockey David Allan will face an immediate decision at the start — if he chases Lady Gormire for the lead, the race shape becomes faster and more complicated; if he drops in, he races out of his natural role with a 0.94 style-fit discount.

The Gay Blade's recent three-win streak and prominent running style make him the most dangerous horse in the favoured shape — watch for him to sit a length or two off Lady Gormire throughout and challenge sharply once the straight begins.

With We've Got This, Yaaser, and Black Storm all true hold-up horses crowded into the rear positions, the straight may see a bunching effect as all three try to find daylight simultaneously — watch for traffic issues in the final 2f that may flatter or cost any of them.

Good to Firm going (confirmed by the going report) suits horses with clean, efficient action over 7f — any runner whose recent wins came on softer ground (notably The Gay Blade's Soft win) should be assessed carefully for whether today's surface is truly their optimal condition.

races.name: Hays Travel Holiday Outside The Box Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Falaise Blanc
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer at 12-13f on good ground for Katie Scott, with six runs showing strong recent form (2-2-4-2 in last four); a natural hold-up horse who will be shuffled to the rear end of what is an already hold-up-heavy field, meaning getting a clean passage to use her finishing effort is the key challenge here.

runners_data.name: Fleur de Mer
runners_data.note: Martin Todhunter's six-year-old has course and distance entries at similar trips but current form on soft-leaning ground means good-to-firm conditions are a potential concern; races hold-up but with the rear so congested, she will find herself racing in mid-division without her preferred target to aim at in the straight.

runners_data.name: Forever Perfect
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' lightly-raced three-year-old has genuine form credentials — a recent winner over 12f at Standard and placed multiple times — and has every chance of getting a clean tracking position behind the lone front-runner as the only unredistributed hold-up type with recent winning form at the distance.

runners_data.name: Hansteen
runners_data.note: John & Sean Quinn yard coming into form (2/10 in 14 days) and Jason Hart takes the ride, which adds jockey quality; won over 12f on good ground earlier this season and this step back up in trip to 12.5f is interesting, though he is a natural hold-up horse who should find a clean position given only modest competition for the back slots.

runners_data.name: Max Of Stars
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears' six-year-old has an excellent record in similar ground conditions (12/15 runs on good, 3W7P) and is the confirmed lone pace-setter, giving him full tactical control at 1m4½f; Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claimer) takes over and needs to ensure he doesn't go too slow and allow runners to creep into contention unchecked.

runners_data.name: Mr Withington
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans' five-year-old has a poor recent record — six, seven, seven, eight in last four — and showed nothing last time over distances short of today's trip; his natural hold-up style means he is bumped to midfield on the map given the overcrowded rear, and the form line gives little encouragement he can benefit even from a favourable position.

runners_data.name: Penelope's Sister
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old has been running over distances shorter than today's 12.5f in recent outings (8f-10f), making this trip step up a concern; a true hold-up runner who is likely to occupy the genuine back-end position, but best form came over longer and the going here (good to firm) has not been her dominant condition.

runners_data.name: Ravenscraig Castle
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen takes the ride on Iain Jardine's eight-year-old who has solid recent form at 16f on good and good-to-soft ground (2nd, 3rd, 4th recently); comes back in trip today from his preferred 16-18f range, but has winning form at 16f and the hold-up style should find a clear run given he is one of the truer hold-up types in the field.

runners_data.name: Sophiesticate
runners_data.note: R Mike Smith's seven-year-old is admirably consistent at 12f on good ground, placing in three of last four at that trip; races hold-up but is one of six-plus runners nudged away from the rear on the map — she will need to work around midfield traffic to deliver her late effort, and the pattern of near-misses rather than wins tempers expectation.

runners_data.name: Storm On Jura
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old is flagged as a fader in the finish, a significant concern in a race at 12.5f where the hold-up horses need sustained stamina; bumped to midfield on the map as one of several displaced rear-runners, recent form figures (0, 9, 6, 4, 8) give no encouragement and the fade flag makes a finish into the frame unlikely.

runners_data.name: Talking In Kode
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's three-year-old is in excellent form (7/7 runs on good ground) with jockey Cian Horgan (5lb) taking the ride; however, recent runs have all been over 8-10f on good ground, making today's 12.5f a significant stamina question, and the hold-up style — pushed to midfield on the map — means he needs every furlong of the trip to be within his range.

runners_data.name: Time Twister
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this Easterby three-year-old who has been off 292 days — a major fitness flag that must dominate any assessment; best form has been over 8-10f, making today's 12.5f another uncertainty, and with only good-going efforts at shorter distances to draw on, this race looks a step too far in terms of both absence and trip.

races.paceDynamic: Max Of Stars is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge him, will control tempo from the outset over 1m4½f on good-to-firm ground at Musselburgh. He sets a sustainable, owner-dictated gallop that is unlikely to be pressured, meaning the race will be run at an honest but measured pace with Max Of Stars potentially stealing an advantage at the top of the straight. That tactical advantage heavily favours horses who can sit just off the pace in prominent positions and quicken from a close-range tracking position, rather than deep closers who need a truly searching tempo to close ground late. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Fleur de Mer, Talking In Kode, Mr Withington, Sophiesticate, Storm On Jura, Hansteen, and Falaise Blanc are all natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is oversubscribed; Forever Perfect, Ravenscraig Castle, and Penelope's Sister are the truest hold-up runners likely to occupy the back end in practice.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Max Of Stars Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Max Of Stars bowls clear unchallenged and the hold-up-heavy field fails to generate enough early pressure to expose the pace.
scenarios.body: Max Of Stars controls every fraction on his own terms, ensuring mid-race tempo stays moderate and that his rivals spend most of the race chasing air; any horse who can track within two lengths of him becomes the primary beneficiary when he ties up late or, if he stays on, those closest to him at the furlong pole take the spoils.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Max Of Stars sets the pace but a horse tracking him in second or third produces a decisive move rounding the home turn.
scenarios.body: The measured gallop means the gap between leader and field remains small enough for a well-placed prominent or close-tracking runner to overhaul Max Of Stars in the final two furlongs without needing exceptional stamina; horses with course/distance form on good-to-firm and a jockey who commits early are best placed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively quick enough mid-race to string the field out and open a clear passage for a back-marker on the rail.
scenarios.body: A genuine hold-up horse who finds a clean run around the final bend could finish strongly into a tiring field, but this requires the tempo to be faster than Max Of Stars' history suggests and for the midfield traffic to part — a low-probability combination in a race mapped with so many runners out of their preferred position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse Of Front
scenarios.trigger: If Max Of Stars is pressured unexpectedly early by a runner moving up aggressively, causing the pace to spike and then collapse.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-anticipated early gallop would burn off the lone pace-setter and leave the field in chaos approaching the straight, ultimately favouring a fresh-legged closer who has been completely unpressured; this outcome is unlikely given the absence of a genuine second pace-maker.

watchPoints.text: Max Of Stars — if Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claimer) allows the tempo to drift too slow in the first half mile, he could face a wall of horses challenging him turning for home; monitor whether he asserts early enough to build a decisive break.

Forever Perfect — the most likely tracker of the pace given unredistributed hold-up style and recent winning form at the distance, but watch for traffic issues if the mid-division becomes congested with redistributed hold-up runners racing out of role.

Ravenscraig Castle (Andrew Mullen) — dropping back from preferred 16-18f trips and stepping into a race where the rear is heavily subscribed; if he gets boxed in behind the midfield pack, his hold-up style cannot function effectively at this shorter trip.

Time Twister — 292 days off is a significant layoff to flag before betting; if she shows signs of fitness in the paddock and moves well, her yard (Easterby) occasionally produces fit returners, but the absence combined with the trip extension makes her high-risk.

Storm On Jura — the 'fades in finish' tag in a 12.5f handicap on good-to-firm ground is a concrete watch-out; if she is well-backed, the flag suggests the late effort will likely not be sustained and punters should be cautious about any drift in price suggesting late money.

races.name: Edinburgh Childrens Hospital Charity Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Albegone
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old Tim Easterby runner who has placed on Good ground this season and carries course experience, but is a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield mapping — on a sharp 5f with a controlled pace this style is unlikely to get adequate time or room to deliver late.|

runners_data.name: Hard Nut
runners_data.note: Aged nine, lowest-rated in the field at OR=45, and Linda Perratt's yard is 0/17 in the last 14 days — a deep closer whose best recent finishes have come in softer ground, and the fast conditions here are a concern; naturally settles right at the back, forced into a midfield role that does not suit.|

runners_data.name: Henery Hawk
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type repositioned into midfield by the weight of closers in this race — his sole win came on Standard (AW) and his three Good-ground runs this term yielded two thirds, though he has never won on genuine turf Good and the redistribution of his race role is the core problem.|

runners_data.name: Hi Lord
runners_data.note: Barry McHugh rides a 4-year-old with a win and three places on Good ground and solid Musselburgh form; a natural hold-up runner who sits back and finishes, and the 8-day turnaround looks fine — gets a prominent jockey booking which could help him travel wider for a run.|

runners_data.name: Jm Jhingree
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans-trained 4-year-old with a win over course and distance on Good this term, T14 strike rate of 3/16 offers trainer momentum; prominent type who should naturally engage close to Keldeo and whose finishing effort is well-suited to a smoothly-run 5f on fast ground.|

runners_data.name: Keldeo
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears runner returning after 35 days, two wins from 10 runs on Good ground and strong course form; the sole confirmed front-runner who will set an uncontested tempo, and the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that as a P-type in a field full of hold-up horses he is racing closer to the front than rivals but his own role is natural — he simply cannot afford to be caught flat.|

runners_data.name: Marajito
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 4-year-old has two wins on Good ground including a course win, the yard is firing at 9/72 in 14 days, and 16 days between runs is fine; a hold-up type whose winning form came when producing a strong late run — the question is whether the Good to Firm pace at 5f is quick enough to stretch the field and create the gap he needs.|

runners_data.name: Peregrine Falcon
runners_data.note: Paddy Bradley takes the ride on Patrick Morris's 4-year-old, who has placed three times over this course and trip on Standard ground but has limited turf form and returns from 47 days off — placed into midfield by the overload of closers, whereas his natural inclination is to sit deep, a combination that looks problematic on fast turf here.|

runners_data.name: Sixcor
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's 8-year-old has consistent placed form on Good ground at 5f including a third over course and distance, though OR=45 is the equal-lowest and the yard's recent 14-day figures are poor (0/17); technically a hold-up horse whose midfield map position is a forced compromise given the closers' queue.|

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan partners Jim Goldie's 5-year-old, who has an exceptional similar-going record of 13/15 qualifying runs and has placed eight times over 5f on Good including three wins — a genuine P-type who will press Keldeo and is the standout beneficiary if the race is run as a smooth-paced prominent contest.|

races.paceDynamic: Keldeo is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 5f handicap on Good to Firm ground at Musselburgh, and with no other genuine pace horse to press them, Harry Russell can dictate a comfortable, measured tempo from the front without being harassed. Woohoo and Jm Jhingree are the two genuine prominent types who will push forward to track Keldeo closely, creating a compressed early order with the bulk of the field — Hi Lord, Marajito, Albegone, and the redistributed hold-up horses — pouring out behind. The field contains significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Peregrine Falcon, Henery Hawk, Albegone, and Sixcor are true closers all mapped forward into midfield because they cannot all settle where they naturally want to be, meaning genuine late finishing room is contested and the true deep closers will be shuffled. A controlled, honest pace set by Keldeo on fast ground at a sharp 5f course heavily favours horses who race prominently or can track the pace and produce one sustained effort — hold-up horses face a compressed finishing run with nowhere to come from.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Keldeo Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Keldeo dictates a smooth, uncontested tempo and the prominent horses Woohoo and Jm Jhingree track efficiently, the race is run to suit those with early position.
scenarios.body: Keldeo sets a fair gallop into the short Musselburgh straight, Woohoo and Jm Jhingree engage from a stalking position and produce a sustained drive that the deeper hold-up types cannot overhaul in the limited run-in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Keldeo Leads All The Way
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely modest and no prominent rival has the pace to reel in Keldeo through the final two furlongs on fast ground.
scenarios.body: Keldeo has already won over 6f on Good at a low OR and hits this race off a 35-day freshener, and a slow-burn pace on a track that does suit front-runners would allow them to steal enough that the closers simply run out of ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected — perhaps Woohoo or Jm Jhingree push Keldeo harder than anticipated — and the field strings out, creating a slipstream for a genuine closer.
scenarios.body: Marajito or Hi Lord, both of whom have course form and have won over 5f on similar ground, could be produced with a late challenge if early positions compress the front group; however, the redistribution of multiple closers into midfield means finishing lanes are congested and the scenario is far less clean.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses contest for prominent positions at the break and an unexpectedly strong early pace causes the front group to tire in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This is an outlier given only one confirmed front-runner, but if both Woohoo and Jm Jhingree throw down on Keldeo hard from the gates, an untidy early scramble could fatigue the leaders and hand a redistributed type like Albegone or Henery Hawk a rare slice of fortune.

watchPoints.text: Woohoo's going record (13/15 on similar ground, 3 wins) combined with Paul Mulrennan's positive booking and natural prominent style make them the key tracking threat to Keldeo — watch whether they take up second position immediately off the gate.

Keldeo's 35-day absence means watch how they jump and whether Harry Russell lets them bowl along naturally or over-steadies — any hesitation at the break and Woohoo or Jm Jhingree could steal a march and effectively lead.

Jm Jhingree is prominent-type with yard momentum (T14: 3/16) and a course-and-distance win on Good this season — if they get a clean break alongside Keldeo the early pace could be quicker than the lone front-runner scenario implies, which would alter the shape toward Scenario C.

The congestion of hold-up types (Albegone, Henery Hawk, Peregrine Falcon, Sixcor, Hard Nut all naturally wanting to settle last) means the draw and early positioning battle behind the front pair will be compressed — watch for traffic trouble in the final two furlongs as multiple closers simultaneously seek gaps.

Marajito's two wins on Good at this course and distance are the form to respect among the hold-up runners, and Tim Easterby's hot 14-day yard form (9/72) is worth noting if you are looking for the most credentialed of the deep closers to outperform the shape.

runners_data.name: Perfidia

runners_data.name: Positive Thoughts
runners_data.note: The only genuine pace-setter in the race for John & Sean Quinn; STYLE_FIT of 0.93 notes it is racing slightly out of its optimal role in this field shape, but the absence of any challenger for the lead means it can dictate entirely on its own terms from the front — a significant advantage despite modest sim-going figures.

races.paceDynamic: Positive Thoughts is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rivals to challenge for the lead, should dictate comfortably from the outset on Good to Firm ground over 1m1f at Musselburgh. The hold-up contingent is numerous — War Memorial, Toy Soldier, Bajan Bandit, and Approaching Dawn all want to come from behind — meaning Positive Thoughts faces zero early pressure and can set a controlled, measured gallop that risks turning this into a sprint finish off a slow pace. Three horses tagged as redistributed (Approaching Dawn, Samra Star, Pebble Dash) are genuine hold-up types who cannot all secure their natural rearward berth; the two prominent types best placed to capitalise on the manufactured tempo are Perfidia and Book Of Life, who can sit just behind Positive Thoughts and be delivered with a meaningful run. This race shape firmly favours prominent racers who can track a solo front-runner and pounce entering the home straight, as the hold-up horses face the dual problem of ground-aided pace and a genuinely solo leader dictating an uncontested tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Positive Thoughts Dictates Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Positive Thoughts controls the race from the front at a measured pace, forcing hold-up horses into a one-run finish.
scenarios.body: Positive Thoughts sets a comfortable fractions on Good to Firm, and Perfidia or Book Of Life tuck in second or third and are produced with a well-timed challenge in the home straight; the hold-up runners never get the searching gallop they need to deliver a telling late burst. Perfidia's strong course and going figures (12/15 sim-going, 2W) make her ideally suited to tracking a solo leader and quickening from a prominent position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Runners Close Late
scenarios.trigger: If Positive Thoughts sets a stronger-than-expected pace or the prominent horses pressure the front, creating enough of a test to bring the closers into play.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested gallop would stretch the race out and give War Memorial, who has a solid win record at 7f-8f on Good, or Approaching Dawn, a returning course winner, the conditions they need to finish past tiring rivals. However, with Approaching Dawn and Samra Star redistrubuted from their natural rearward spots and unlikely to settle as far back as preferred, pure hold-up scenarios carry structural risk.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Helps Pace
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent and mid-division horses dispute positions early, creating a more genuine pace that opens the race up.
scenarios.body: Book Of Life and Perfidia both wanting prominent berths behind a lone front-runner could create minor early jostling, lifting the tempo slightly and suiting a horse who can sit just off the pace and respond when challenged in the straight. Perfidia's trainer Tim Easterby is in strong form (T14:9/72) and Book Of Life's placed record on similar going (0W1P sim-going) gives both angles here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Defies Pace Map
scenarios.trigger: If pace collapses entirely in the straight and a lower-rated, out-of-role horse runs into an unexpected placing.
scenarios.body: Pebble Dash or Samra Star, both redistributed from their natural hold-up positions into midfield, could accidentally benefit if the pace falls apart in the final furlong and they find themselves in an uncharacteristically competitive position. Neither carries meaningful form on Good going (Samra Star 0W1P, Pebble Dash 0W0P sim-going) and this scenario relies on chaos rather than merit.

watchPoints.text: Perfidia's ability to track Positive Thoughts and mount a prominent challenge is the single biggest shape threat — watch how quickly she moves to sit second in the early stages, as that position will define the race.

Toy Soldier's flagged tendency to fade in the finish means punters should watch the final furlong closely; if this horse takes up a prominent position it may stop sharply and inconvenience challengers coming from behind.

Cian Horgan rides both Book Of Life and Bajan Bandit for Patrick Morris — he can only ride one, so confirm the final jockey allocations before race off as it changes the prominence picture behind Positive Thoughts.

With Approaching Dawn, Samra Star, and Pebble Dash all redistributed from their natural rear-of-field positions, watch the early stages for bunching in the back half of the field — traffic problems mid-race are a genuine risk for all three.

War Memorial's step up from 7f to 1m1f only eight days after its last run is worth monitoring in the paddock; if the horse looks fresh and well, the extra furlong may suit, but a tired appearance would confirm the short-turnaround risk.
